thesis: Two near-quitting stories show how rapid growth and project overruns can create severe operational and emotional strain.
summary: The participant recounts a student-storage peak season with vehicle accidents, customer complaints, and inadequate delegation. A separate ground-up storage development exceeded its budget and schedule, requiring difficult requests for additional bank and investor funding. The stories qualify a simple success narrative by describing fear, reputational exposure, and the burden of responsibility. The interview also names the emotional cost of letting a long-serving employee go. Claims linking income directly to stress tolerance and estimating who should become an entrepreneur are opinions, not demonstrated general relationships.

insights.title: Test delivery capacity alongside demand generation
insights.explanation: The speaker's successful local marketing produced more customers than the existing warehouse and staffing setup could comfortably handle. The episode illustrates that more demand can expose operating weaknesses.
insights.quote: i had to rent 20,000 extra feet to put them in

insights.title: Allow for financing consequences of overruns
insights.explanation: The reported project rose from a 1.7 million budget to about 2.45 million and ran late. The consequence described is returning to both investors and the bank for more funding, not merely an accounting variance.
insights.quote: I had to go back to my investors and ask for 20% more money
insights.speaker: unresolved

insights.title: Include emotional costs when assessing entrepreneurship
insights.explanation: The participant describes anxiety before investor conversations and distress over employee departures. His eventual success does not erase those experiences or establish that everyone should accept them.
insights.quote: I have been humbled by entrepreneurship
